transcription.tex: \text{Add, subtract and scale vectors. Show that vectors are parallel by expressing one as a scalar multiple of the other.}
\text{Calculate lengths, directions and unit vectors using components.}
\text{Describe points relative to an origin; solve problems involving ratios, parallel lines and intersections.}

transcription.tex: \text{A vector describes a displacement. It has both magnitude (length) and direction.}
\text{\(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) means the displacement from P to Q.}
\text{Vectors with the same magnitude and direction are equal, wherever they are drawn.}
\text{Following one displacement and then another gives their resultant.}
\text{Reversing the journey preserves the magnitude and reverses the direction.}

transcription.tex: \text{6. OPQ is a triangle. R lies on PQ with \(2\overrightarrow{PR}=\overrightarrow{RQ}\), and \(\overrightarrow{OS}=3\overrightarrow{OR}\). Given \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\mathbf a\) and \(\overrightarrow{OQ}=\mathbf b\):}
\text{\[\overrightarrow{OR}=\mathbf a+\tfrac13(\mathbf b-\mathbf a)\]\[=\tfrac23\mathbf a+\tfrac13\mathbf b\]\[\overrightarrow{OS}=3\overrightarrow{OR}=2\mathbf a+\mathbf b\]}
\text{(b) T satisfies \(\overrightarrow{OT}=-\mathbf b\). Prove that T, P and S lie on a straight line.}

\text{\[\overrightarrow{TP}=\mathbf a-(-\mathbf b)=\mathbf a+\mathbf b\]\[\overrightarrow{PS}=(2\mathbf a+\mathbf b)-\mathbf a=\mathbf a+\mathbf b\]TP and PS are equal vectors sharing the point P, so T, P and S are collinear.}

transcription.tex: \text{[STEP 2010 Q7] O, A and B are not collinear. Let \(\mathbf c=\alpha\mathbf a+\beta\mathbf b\), where \(\alpha,\beta>0\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\). P = OA ∩ BC and Q = OB ∩ AC.}

\text{Show that \(\mathbf p=\frac{\alpha\mathbf a}{1-\beta}\) and find q. Show that \(\mathbf r=\frac{\alpha\mathbf a+\beta\mathbf b}{\alpha+\beta}\) lies on OC and AB. If S = OB ∩ PR, prove OQ/BQ = OS/BS.}
\text{\[\mathbf p=\mathbf b+t(\mathbf c-\mathbf b)\]\[1+t(\beta-1)=0\Rightarrow t=\frac1{1-\beta}\]\[\mathbf p=\frac\alpha{1-\beta}\mathbf a,\qquad\mathbf q=\frac\beta{1-\alpha}\mathbf b\]}
\text{\[\mathbf r=\frac{\mathbf c}{\alpha+\beta}\]\[\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\frac\beta{\alpha+\beta}(\mathbf b-\mathbf a)\]The first expression places R on OC; the second places R on AB.}

\text{\[\mathbf s=\mathbf p+u(\mathbf r-\mathbf p)\]The coefficient of a is zero, giving\[\mathbf s=\frac\beta{\alpha+2\beta-1}\mathbf b.\]\[\frac{OQ}{BQ}=\frac\beta{1-\alpha-\beta}\]\[\frac{OS}{BS}=\frac{|\beta/(\alpha+2\beta-1)|}{|1-\beta/(\alpha+2\beta-1)|}\]\[=\frac\beta{1-\alpha-\beta}.\]}
\text{The stated intersection S exists when \(\alpha+2\beta\ne1\). Otherwise PR is parallel to OB.}
